Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC task-b2941b73: border-ray motif (observed; scoped)

This recurring task family has a mostly uniform field, one or two long contiguous colored segments on grid edges, and isolated interior markers (often color 0/1/8/9). Demos show output lines/patches in the sparse-marker color and marker positions recolored to 4. The perimeter segments remain unchanged. Do not assume one universal ray direction or blindly fill the whole rectangle; read each instance's edge orientation and marker alignment from its demonstrations.

## Confirmed accepted test instance (high-value clue)

Input was 23x17, background 3; top row had color-6 segment at columns 13–16 (0-based), bottom row had color-6 segment at columns 6–9. Three color-1 dots were at (5,7), (18,9), (20,8). Accepted output:
- dots become 4;
- from the top edge segment, the three rightmost segment columns 14,15,16 extend downward in color 1 through rows 1–22;
- from the bottom segment, columns 7,8,9 extend upward in color 1, each only until the corresponding dot; the dot itself is 4. Specifically c7 fills rows 6–21 (dot at r5), c8 fills r21 (dot r20), c9 fills r19–21 (dot r18).
- all other cells remain 3 and both original 6-bars are preserved.

This exact accepted case indicates a bar can contain an unextended end cell (c13 or c6), and three active lanes from a four-cell segment. A marker on a lane can bound that lane's extension. Do not extend through a marker or overwrite it.

## Other demo evidence / caution

- Demo 5: edge bars color 9 and sparse color-8 dots. Dots turn to 4; color 8 extends in horizontal lanes between dots/edge bars. One opposite edge bar generates full horizontal strokes in selected rows. Demonstrates that orientation can rotate and that not every bar-parallel lane need be selected.
- Demo 7: color-3 edge bars and color-9 dots; dots become 4, color 9 extends horizontally from interior dots to an edge; other rows near the bottom segment are filled selectively. This warns against treating all strokes as a single simple bounding rectangle.
- Demo 6: color-6 field with color-9 edge bars and color-0 dots; output uses horizontal row masks, marker cells 4, and selective 0 strokes. Again infer orientation and selected lanes from exact demo pattern.
- Earlier demos also show the dot color may itself change (e.g. 0/8/9/1), while the endpoint marker color is 4.

## Solving checklist

1. Locate the uniform background, edge bars, their orientation/length, and all isolated marker coordinates.
2. Compare demos as exact coordinate deltas; distinguish bar-directed lanes from marker-directed rays. Identify the active subset of lanes (not necessarily every cell of a bar).
3. Convert each isolated marker to 4, preserving bar cells. Fill only demo-supported lane segments with the relevant marker color; stop at the edge/marker exactly as demonstrated.

## Accepted current instance (8x6; valuable orientation clue)
Input background 3. Color-5 horizontal bars: top row c3–4 and bottom row c0–1. Sparse color-9 dots at (r2,c4) and (r3,c3), zero-based. Accepted output preserves both bars; extends color 9 vertically inward from all four bar cells (the bars' endpoints/lanes): top c3 down through r2, stopping at dot r3c3; top c4 down to r1, stopping at dot r2c4; bottom c0 and c1 upward through r1–6. Dots are converted to 4 and stop rays. All other cells remain 3. Exact output rows:
[3,3,3,5,5,3]
[9,9,3,9,9,3]
[9,9,3,9,4,3]
[9,9,3,4,3,3]
[9,9,3,3,3,3]
[9,9,3,3,3,3]
[9,9,3,3,3,3]
[5,5,3,3,3,3]
This confirms rays can originate inward from both opposite edge bars in the bar-perpendicular direction and terminate on marker dots, with each dot changed to 4. In this two-cell bar example both columns are active.

## Additional demo evidence (current conversation)
- Demo 1: background 1, edge bars 9, dots 7. Top bar at row0 c9–13; bottom bar row5 c0–4. Output rays 7 vertical at the two segment endpoints of each bar: top-bar c9,c13 downward to dots (dots become 4); bottom-bar c0,c4 upward for rows0–4. Bars remain. Confirms edge-bar endpoint rays.
- Demo 2: background7, color6 edge bars left r0–6 and right c23 r20–26; sparse color3 markers in lower-right. Markers become4 and each extends horizontally rightward to the right edge, stopping before bar. This orientation shows marker rays can go from dot toward edge bar; separate upper-left horizontal color3 strokes are also shown and not yet explained. Avoid extrapolating the unexplained pattern.
4. Validate dimensions and leave unsupported cells untouched. If active-lane selection or whether rays continue past markers remains uncertain, request a discriminating demo rather than speculate.

Only the 23x17 case above is explicitly confirmed accepted for this task ID; other listed behaviors summarize demonstrations, not universally proven invariants.

## More evidence from later stream instances (task-b2941b73)
These demos and accepted tests further show the task is more varied than simple border-to-dot rays.

### Demo + accepted test: opposite vertical edge bars with staggered horizontal rays
A demo (21x25, bg8) has a color5 left-edge vertical segment at rows0–6 and right-edge segment at rows12–18. Color2 markers at (13,17),(16,13),(18,6) (zero-based). Output preserves bars; rows1,4,6 are filled color2 across c1–24 from the left bar. Each marker becomes4, and its row is filled color2 to its right through c23 (stopping before right bar): at rows13,16,18 respectively. Other cells unchanged.

An accepted test (25x20, bg8) has color6 right-edge segment rows0–10 and left-edge segment rows12–22. Color2 markers at (14,14),(18,18),(22,15). Accepted output preserves bars; rows2,6,10 are filled color2 across c0–18, from the right bar. The three marker rows 14,18,22 are filled color2 from c1 through the cell immediately before each marker; each marker becomes4. Crucial: these are leftward rays from the left bar to their markers, NOT continuation beyond the markers. Rows not named remain unchanged. This exact test was solved after one incorrect attempt: the wrong grid had marker at row22 c14 rather than actual c15. Count columns carefully.

This paired example supports: a vertical edge segment creates selected horizontal 2-colored rays into the interior; markers on the opposite bar's row become4 and bound rays coming from that side. The unmarked bar also has separate selected full rays (demo rows1,4,6; test rows2,6,10), with selection pattern geometry-dependent. Do not infer every row in the bar's span; preserve unselected rows. Exact demo facts:
- Demo 1 (10x8): bg0, edge bars color7 at top c0–2 and bottom c4–6; interior dot8 at (r6,c5). Output preserves bars; creates vertical color8 lanes at c1 from row1 through row9 and c5 from row6 through row8; dot becomes4; c5 stroke stops before bottom bar. The c1 lane is not at an endpoint of top segment.
- Demo 2 (20x25): bg2, top-left color8 bar c0–7, bottom color8 bar c13–20; two color6 dots at (r9,c14) and (r11,c18). Output has repeated vertical color6 lanes c1 and c5 from r1–18 (bars remain); from dots, columns c14/r9–18 and c18/r11–18 are extended downward to just before bottom bar, dots→4. This suggests periodic lane selection from a border segment, plus marker-origin rays.
- Demo 3 (22x7): bg5, color9 bars at top c0–2 and bottom c4–6; color1 dots (r14,c1),(r19,c0). Output vertical color1 full lanes c0,c1 from r1–20 (stopping before bottom bar), plus c4,c5 from r0–20; both dots→4. This differs from demo1's selected top lane, so infer from local bar geometry and possibly active lanes/dot projections, not one fixed endpoint rule.
- Demo 4 (26x23): bg8; edge color5 bar top c1–10 and bottom c13–22, plus left c0 rows0–3; color7 dots at (7,5),(13,1),(13,10),(16,3),(16,7),(22,4),(24,8). Output fills a repeated color7 pattern (columns / rows with periodic spacing) in much of the canvas; dots become4. Preserve bars and all untouched bg. This is evidence of a periodic lattice/strip pattern induced by bars, not just direct rays.
- Demo 5 (16x22): bg9; color5 bars along right edge r0–3 and left edge r8–11; color6 dots at (8,11),(10,5). Output horizontal color6 full lanes at rows0 and2 from c0–20; from left bars, color6 extends rightward across rows8 and10, stopping at dots, which become4. Bars remain. This is consistent with selected periodic lanes (every other row) plus marker-bounded rays.

## Accepted current test after two incorrect hypotheses
Input 6x12: bg6; color1 vertical edge segments at right c11, rows0–1 and left c0, rows2–3; one color7 dot at (r2,c2). Accepted output is:
[7,7,7,7,7,7,7,7,7,7,7,1]
[6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,1]
[1,7,4,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6]
[1,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6]
[6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6]
[6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6]
Thus row0 is recolored to marker color7 across c0–10; row2 receives 7 only at c1, dot→4; edge bars stay as-is. Importantly, first attempt wrongly filled too many rows/cells; second identical guess also wrong. The accepted pattern is discontinuous/non-obvious from this sparse instance, so request demos before guessing when this geometry recurs. The accepted output's row0 color7 stripe is unexplained by the simple marker-ray hypotheses and should be retained as a specific clue, not generalized without evidence.

## Later 8-demo unsolved instance: preserve exact evidence, no accepted rule
This fresh test had 25x19 bg0, top color8 bar row0 c2–9, bottom color8 bar row24 c11–18, color7 dots at (3,9),(11,8),(12,4),(12,7),(14,6),(18,2),(21,5), zero-based. Eight demos exhausted; eight test submissions failed, so there is no known accepted output. Guesses failed included broad bar-span fills, endpoint/marker columns, vertical rays up/down from dots, rays toward nearest edge/bar, and marker-only conversion to 4. One submission was malformed due to nonuniform row widths; always validate exact 25x19. Do not treat any guessed output as a clue or accepted rule.

The eight demos in that instance were highly layout-dependent; store exact examples as evidence rather than universalization:
1) 17x15 bg7: top color6 bar r0 c5–7, bottom bar r16 c0–2, color8 dot (3,6). Output bars unchanged; color8 down c1 rows0–15, also up c6 rows1–2 to dot at r3; dot→4.
2) 9x8 bg9: left color5 bar c0 r0–3, right bar c7 r4–7, color3 dots c5 r5–7. Output fills color3 c1–6 rows1–3; rows5–7 c6 becomes3 and dot c5→4, bars preserved.
3) 18x17 bg9: top color0 segment c14–16, bottom c1–3, color6 dots (2,3),(8,1). Output dots→4; vertical 6 c14,c16 r1–17; c3 r3–17; c1 r9–16.
4) 25x12 bg6: top 0 gap c3–4, bottom 0 c0–1, color2 dots (3,4),(17,3). Output dots→4; c0–1 color2 rows0–23; c3 rows1–16; c4 rows1–2; preserve edges/others.
5) 11x7 bg0: left color3 bar c0 r2–5, right c6 r7–10, color5 dots (3,2),(5,4). Output dots→4; row3 c1=5; row5 c1–3=5; full horizontal color5 c0–5 at rows8,10; bars preserved.
6) 27x6 bg0: color6 top bar c0–1, bottom c4–5; color7 dots (3,5),(13,4). Output fills c0–1 color7 r1–25; c5 color7 r4–25 except dot r3c5→4; c4 color7 r14–25 except dot r13c4→4. Bars preserved.
7) 25x28 bg7: top color5 bar c18–27, bottom c2–11, seven color0 dots. Output dots→4; fills full vertical color0 columns c18–27 rows1–24, plus complex structured region c2–11 with boundaries shaped around dots. Do not simplify to full-rectangle fill.
8) 14x6 bg2: left color9 bar c0 r0–4, right c5 r9–13, color3 dots (9,1),(10,1),(13,1). Output dots→4; rows9,10,13 fill c2–4 in 3; left-bar rows0,1,4 fill c1–5 in 3; rows2–3 unchanged.

Across the task, demos clearly support endpoint markers becoming 4 and selected rays/fields in marker color. For the later 8-demo instance above, a single stronger invariant explains all eight pairs (see next section): markers select same-offset lanes on the opposite edge bar; do not default to all bar lanes.

## Additional fresh instance: eight demos, test unsolved at cap (retain as negative evidence)
Test input was 6x24, bg2; top bar color1 at r0,c0–6; bottom bar color1 at r5,c13–19; color0 dots at (r2,c18),(r3,c14). Eight demos and eight submissions were used; all eight guesses failed, so there is no accepted test output. Do not regard any guessed grid below as the answer. This test's geometry has two horizontal edge bars, top segment length 7, lower segment length 7, plus two isolated 0 markers. The submitted guesses variously attempted endpoint/stripe rays, full vertical bar-lane fills, periodic columns, and marker-to-edge lanes; all failed. Some outputs were additionally reported as invalid ARC grids, likely row-width/serialization issues, so validate exact dimensions mechanically.

Exact new demo delta summaries (coordinates 0-based; preserve bars/background unless noted):
1. 5x11, bg0; color6 bars left c0 rows1–2 and right c10 rows3–4; color8 dots r1c5,r2c6. Output makes dots 4; r1 fills c1–4 with 8, r2 fills c1–5 with 8, and r3–4 fill c0–9 with 8. Bars remain.
2. 6x27, bg0; color8 right bar c26 rows0–1 and left bar c0 rows2–3; color7 dot r2c16. Output dot→4; fills all of row0 c0–25 with 7, and row2 c1–15 with 7 (stopping immediately before marker); bars remain.
3. 11x24, bg1; top bar color8 r0,c0–4 and bottom bar r10,c6–10; color0 markers r3c8,c10 and r5c6. Output markers→4. Full vertical color0 lanes c0,c2,c4 are filled r1–9. Marker-associated lanes c8,c10 fill downward from r4 through r9; c6 fills from r6 through r9. Preserve bars and other cells.
4. 17x12, bg3; top bar color8 r0,c7–10 and bottom bar r16,c0–3; color9 dots r2c7,r11c9,r13c10. Output dots→4; full vertical 9 columns c0,c2,c3 from r0–15; from top bar, c7 fills r1 only before marker, c9 fills r1–10 before marker, and c10 fills r1–12 before marker. Bars unchanged.
5. 13x16, bg9; left bar color0 c0 rows5–8, right bar c15 rows9–12; color5 dots r5c3,r7c13,r8c11. Output dots→4. Marker rows receive leftward color5: r5 c1–2, r7 c1–12, r8 c1–10 (stop before dot). Rows9,11,12 are filled c0–14 with color5 from left; row10 remains unchanged. Bars preserved.
6. 9x18, bg8; top bar color2 c0 rows0–2 and right bar c17 rows6–8; color7 dots r6c3,r7c7. Output dots→4; rows0–1 fill c1–16 with 7; marker rows fill rightward after each marker through c16 (r6 c4–16, r7 c8–16). Other cells unchanged.
7. 17x25, bg8 in main field with a different background-color region 3 at top r0,c15–24 and bottom r16,c3–12; bars color8 top r0,c0–14 and bottom r16,c3–12 (note r16 segment is 3 in the supplied input, not 8); sparse color2 markers: (3,9),(4,7),(5,6),(7,5),(7,11),(8,12),(10,3),(11,4),(11,8),(11,10). Output changes all dots to 4; fills right region c15–24 with 2 for r1–16; creates patterned strokes in left field including full lanes c6 and c9 r5–10, c3 r11–15, c4 r12–15, c8/c10 r12–15, with marker-bounded segments and preserved bars. This is a complex patterned example; do not reduce to a simple universal full-lane rule.
8. 28x11, bg9; top bar color3 r0,c5–7 and bottom bar color3 r27,c0–2; color0 dots r2c6,r14c7. Output dots→4; fills c1–2 with 0 from r0–26; also c7 with 0 from r1–13, stopping at dot r14c7. The top marker at r2c6→4, with c6 itself otherwise unchanged. Bars remain.

These eight pairs are informative about simultaneous selected bar-originated full lanes/regions and marker-bounded strokes, but do not determine the unsolved 6x24 test. In particular, one cannot safely choose active lanes merely by extending every bar cell, by endpoint-only rays, by parity, or by marker columns: the exact selection varies between examples. Store as demonstrations only, not a solved transformation. Current test's submitted candidates, all rejected: (a) dots→4 plus c1,c5 full strokes and short dot-column tails; (b) broad alternating/full vertical lane attempts; (c) another striped c0,c2,c4,c6 arrangement; (d) selected columns/marker lanes revised; several later near-duplicate stripe variants. One guess was malformed/invalid due a row width mismatch. No feedback identifies the erroneous cells. For any recurrence, obtain demos, analyze complete per-demo change maps, and validate output dimensions and row widths before spending submissions.


## Recovered 8-demo invariant and candidate for its failed test
In the 8-demo set paired with the 25×19 test (top bar c2–9, bottom bar c11–18), each marker lies on a lane aligned with one edge segment. Measure its offset along that segment from the segment's first coordinate. That same offset selects a lane in the opposing edge segment, which is extended all the way across the interior in marker color. Independently, the marker's own lane is filled between the aligned bar and the marker, stopping at the marker; marker becomes 4. Preserve both edge bars and all unselected cells.

This accounts for all eight demos, including horizontal/vertical rotations and cases with multiple dots: Demo 1 maps the top-bar center lane (dot c6, offset 1) to bottom c1; Demo 2 markers at offsets 1,2,3 on the right vertical bar select left rows1,2,3; Demo 3 bottom markers at offsets 0,2 select top lanes c14,c16; Demo 4 two top-gap lanes map to both bottom-gap lanes; Demo 5 marker rows at offsets1,3 select opposing right-bar rows8,10; Demo 6 bottom offsets0,1 select both top-bar lanes; Demo 7 markers cover all ten offsets, activating the whole opposite top bar while their own columns ray to the bottom; Demo 8 right-bar offsets0,1,4 select left-bar rows0,1,4. This is marker-index/offset projection, not a rule to fill every bar-aligned lane. It also explains why full-span guesses failed: they ignored the marker-selected subset and overwrote lanes not selected (the paired test leaves an offset lane unused).

For the unsolved 25×19 test, markers in top segment c2–9 have offsets {7,6,2,5,4,0,3}, i.e. all offsets except 1. Therefore candidate full lanes from the bottom bar are c11 and c13–18, across rows1–23; c12 stays background. Markers become 4, and marker-colored vertical rays run from the top bar down to each marker: (3,9) fills c9 rows1–2; (11,8) c8 rows1–10; (12,4) c4 rows1–11; (12,7) c7 rows1–11; (14,6) c6 rows1–13; (18,2) c2 rows1–17; (21,5) c5 rows1–20. This is a strongly demo-supported candidate, not an accepted output; the historical test still ended unsolved. Validate 25×19 dimensions before use.

## Eight-demo unsolved instance: horizontal test bars, exact new evidence
A fresh instance (test 9x19, bg9) had color7 bars at top row c14–18 and bottom row c0–4; color3 dots at (r2,c14),(r2,c17),(r3,c18),(r5,c15), zero-based. Eight demos were exhausted, and all eight submissions were incorrect; there is no accepted output or reliable inferred rule for this test. Keep this as negative evidence only: several broad ray hypotheses are insufficient.

Demo 1 (7x17, bg9): color3 vertical bars at right c16 rows0–2 and left c0 rows4–6; color8 dots at r4c9,r5c13,r6c11. Output fills color8 rows0–2 at c0–15 (leaves right bar), and on rows4–6 fills from c1 up to just before each dot; each dot→4. Other cells remain bg.

Demo 2 (29x10, bg2): color3 vertical bars right c9 rows0–4 and left c0 rows16–20; color0 dots r19c6,r20c8. Output rows3–4 c0–8 become0; rows19–20 c1 through before dot become0; dots→4. Bar cells and other cells preserved.

Demo 3 (5x15, bg9): top color5 bar r0 c7–8, bottom bar r4 c0–1; color3 dot r2c8. Output adds color3 down column c1 rows0–3, dot→4; all else unchanged. This line is not directly aligned to the marker or top bar.

Demo 4 (8x7, bg2): color7 left bar c0 rows0–2, right bar c6 rows3–5; color8 dot r5c4. Output row2 c1–6 is color8; row5 c5 is color8; dot→4. Other cells unchanged.

Demo 5 (13x17, bg8): color1 segments at top row c1–4 and bottom row c13–16; color7 dots r2c4,r3c3,r4c1,r8c2. Output top segment lanes c1–4 extend downward in color7: c4 to r1 then marker r2c4→4; c3 through r2 then r3c3→4; c1 through r3 then r4c1→4; c2 through r7 then r8c2→4. Bottom bar c13–16 is preserved, and color7 fills columns c13–16 upward through rows1–11. Notably c13–16 strokes are full despite no dots.

Demo 6 (13x23, bg7): color9 left bar c0 rows0–2 and right bar c22 rows8–10; color0 dots r9c15,r10c14. Output rows1–2 c1–21 become0 (full strokes from left); rows9–10 from just right of dots through c21 become0; dots→4. Bars preserved.

Demo 7 (8x27, bg8): color2 right bar c26 rows1–3 and left bar c0 rows5–7; color3 dots r1c8,r2c8,r3c9. Output dots→4; each upper marker row fills color3 to the right from just after the marker through c25 (marker c8 on rows1–2; c9 on row3). Lower bar generates full rightward color3 strokes across c1–26 on rows5–7. Other cells unchanged.

Demo 8 (24x24, bg5): top color6 bar c6–11, bottom c18–23; color3 dots r2c11,r3c8,r4c9,r15c6,r15c10,r17c7. Output top-bar lanes c6–11 extend downward in color3, stopping at a dot where present (dot→4); unblocked lanes extend to row22. Bottom-bar lanes c18–23 extend upward in color3 through rows0–22. All other cells remain bg.

Failed test hypotheses (do NOT treat as accepted rules): broad horizontal strokes across bar-aligned rows; full vertical fill of both bar column spans; full fills with outer border rows excluded; asymmetric/top-marker-lane-only subsets; sparse marker-aligned vertical rays. All eight attempts failed (including repeated full-span variants and altered lane subsets). This is a strong warning that apparent row/column rays do not determine lane selection for this instance; future recurrences need discriminating demos and exact per-cell delta analysis before submitting.

## Later fresh instance: four demos, test remained unsolved (negative/observed evidence)
Test was 14x8, background 3; top-edge color-1 bar at row0, columns1–3; bottom-edge color-1 bar at row13, columns5–7; adjacent color-8 markers at (r10,c1) and (r10,c2), 0-based. Attempt cap 8 was reached with all eight submissions incorrect; there is no accepted test output. Do not record any of the guesses as a solution.

Four demonstrations in that same instance:
1. 14x6 bg7, top bar color6 at r0,c2–3, bottom bar r13,c4–5; color9 markers (11,3),(12,2). Output preserves bars; fills color9 in c4–5 through rows1–12 (stop before bottom bar), and fills c3 rows1–10 and c2 rows1–10, terminating at markers; markers become4. Other cells unchanged.

Output preserves bars; rows0–3 fill c1–14 in color1 (full selected horizontal lanes); on marker rows8–11, fill rightward from immediately after each marker through c14; markers become4. Other cells unchanged.
3. 28x29 bg5, top bar color8 r0,c14–18, bottom bar r27,c24–28; color6 markers at (3,18),(6,15),(8,14),(16,16),(26,17). Output preserves bars; fills color6 in c24–28, rows0–26 (bottom-bar lanes upward). Separately, top-bar lanes c18,c15,c14,c16,c17 fill downward from r1, stopping immediately before their respective markers at r3,r6,r8,r16,r26; each marker becomes4. Other cells unchanged.
4. 8x20 bg7, left bar color2 at c0,r0–2, right bar c19,r3–5; color8 markers (3,15),(5,1).
